title: The Crown of the Sundered Sea
premise: Astrid Yarrow's memory-charms are harmless thefts — stolen moments bottled and sold — until the night a dying priest pays him with a memory of the old gods' covenant and Astrid realizes the magic inside him is the last living shard of dragon-fire. Hunted by the Salt Inquisition and courted by a drowned god who wants the covenant broken forever, Astrid must journey to the Sundered Sea with Sera Vane, the inquisitor ordered to kill him, and choose between restoring the gods at the cost of every memory he has ever stolen — including his love for Sera. He reforges the covenant by surrendering his own past to the flame, ending the drought of magic, though he wakes with no memory of her; the final chapter turns on whether love can be chosen again without memory, and it can.
about_author: Wren Okonkwo is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloging salvaged ship logs off the West African coast before turning to fantasy. They write about memory, salt, and the things people trade to survive, and live within earshot of a working harbor.

chapters.title: The Taste of Borrowed Lightning
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In the smuggler-city of Greyharrow, Astrid sells a stolen first kiss to a grieving widow, establishing his trade and his rules: never steal love, never steal grief. Then a dying priest of the drowned god presses a memory into his hands — and it won't come out. Emotional beat: unease, the first crack in a carefully small life.

chapters.title: What the Priest Drowned Knowing
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The priest's memory reveals the Sundered Covenant: the old gods sleep beneath the sea, fed by dragon-fire, and someone has been extinguishing the flames one by one. Astrid tries to sell the memory and finds no buyer — because Inquisitor Sera Vane is already in the city, asking about him. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Ordered to execute the last fire-thief, Sera instead offers Astrid a deal: help her find who is killing the gods, and she'll lose his file. Their interrogation of a corrupt harbormaster reveals the Inquisition's own Grandmother signed the extinction order. Beat: reluctant alliance, first spark of mutual respect.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Fleeing Greyharrow together, Astrid and Sera cross the ash-lands where magic once flourished and now nothing grows. A memory-wraith attacks Astrid, drawn to the priest's gift, and Sera saves him — breaking every rule of her order. Beat: intimacy born of danger; the road strips away their armor.

chapters.title: The God Who Answers Collect
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The drowned god Nereus speaks to Astrid through stolen memories, offering to restore his childhood — which he sold long ago to survive — if he shatters the covenant and frees the gods to take the world back. Beat: temptation; Astrid confronts how much of himself he has already sold.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Confession
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Captured by the Inquisition and brought before Grandmother, Sera learns the truth: the Inquisition didn't outlaw magic to protect people — it outlawed it to starve the gods, because a god once demanded Sera's own family as payment. Loyalty to her order collides with truth. Beat: betrayal, and the choice to burn her own life down.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the volcanic isle of Cinderveil, they find the final flame guttering, guarded by the last warden — a woman who has kept it alive for two hundred years and recognizes the shard in Astrid. To reforge the covenant, a living memory of love must be fed to the fire. Beat: terrible clarity; the price is finally named.

chapters.title: Everything He Stole, Everything He Kept
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Nereus makes his final offer: give him the shard and Astrid gets his childhood back, his whole stolen past restored, Sera spared the cost. Astrid refuses — some debts should stay paid. Sera, arriving, realizes what the covenant demands and tries to take his place. Beat: love against duty, both refusing to let the other pay.

chapters.title: The Sundering Reforged
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax. Grandmother's fleet attacks Cinderveil; Nereus rises from the sea to claim the shard. In the chaos, Astrid feeds his memories — fifteen years of charms, the priest's gift, his love for Sera — into the dragon-fire. The covenant blazes back to life; the gods wake bound to their bargain; Nereus is pulled under. Beat: sacrifice, awe, and loss.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, then shared. Months later, Greyharrow's magic is legal and small again. Astrid lives quietly, memoryless but unhaunted, and a woman keeps buying charms she doesn't need just to talk to him. In the final scene, he offers her a stolen first kiss — free of charge. Beat: resolution; love chosen again, without memory, is love that lasts.
